newsitem.title: INDIA: India details energy needs for seven pct growth.
newsitem.headline: India details energy needs for seven pct growth.

text.p: India may have to import 65 million tonnes of oil and add 12,000 megawatts of energy annually for the next five years to fuel an economic growth rate of 7 percent, a top administrator said on Tuesday.

P. Abraham, the bureaucrat who heads the power ministry, said India's energy sector, which opened to private enterprise following economic reforms launched in 1991, offered exciting opportunities to international energy industries.

"If the projected growth rate of seven percent plus in GDP (Gross Domestic Product) is to be maintained then by the end of the ninth five-year plan, we may touch 100 MT of oil consumption out of which about 65 MT would have to be imported," Abraham told reporters.
"Also an additional capacity for power generation at the rate of 10,000 to 12,000 MW per year will have to be added to meet the requirements of the industry and the agriculture sector," he added.
Abraham was announcing the agenda for Asia Energy Vision 2020, a three-day energy conference, sponsored by his ministry, which will be held in New Delhi from November 15.
The conference will bring together funding agencies, industrialists and officials for business meetings, he said.
At the Indian Energy Seminar scheduled for the conference, the federal government will present its proposed policies for the next decade, an official statement said.

An estimated 60 energy experts from nearly 30 countries will participate in the conference, along with 400 Indian specialists, to discuss global issues on the energy front to ensure sustainable development, Abraham said.
